decisions.executionNote: Raise and curl both arms in their own workspaces toward red and blue nuts, using small mirrored increments to preserve elbow-up continuity. Will refine alignment from the next views.
Finish orienting grippers vertically above the red and blue nuts. Estimated nut centers from calibrated head rays; maintain overhead clearance before descending.
Descend vertically to the nut grasp height with small centering corrections, then close both grippers. Retention remains to be checked visually on lift.
Lift the visibly enclosed red and blue nuts, then carry each above its same-color screw without crossing workspaces. Keep both grippers closed and check coaxial alignment next.
Lower the retained nuts cautiously to the screw-tip insertion height. Head alignment is close; inspect wrist parallax and contact before applying tightening rotation.
Refine alignment inward and slightly back using the elevated screw-tip rays rather than tabletop centers. Ease down only 3 mm to check that each tip enters its nut bore.
Both tips are now visible within the bores. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with a shallow axial descent and tiny final centering corrections; keep grippers closed.
Release the nuts for a ratcheting reset, returning wrist yaw without lifting or unscrewing them. Check whether both remain seated before the next tightening stroke.
The release exposed that neither nut stayed threaded. Reposition over the displaced nuts to recover them, using the observed tabletop locations and a conservative overhead approach.

Use the wrist views to center the displaced nuts and descend to the previous pickup height, then close. The prior failure may have been insufficient insertion depth; recovery is checked before another attempt.
Lift the recovered nuts to verify retention and carry them back over their matching screw tips. Keep closed throughout; final coaxial placement will use the wrist views.
The red nut rotated in the grasp and the blue nut was not retained. Set the red nut down in clear left space for a flat regrasp, while aligning the open right gripper above the blue nut.
Regrasp at the lower, previously effective nut height after allowing the parts to settle. Close and make a short verification lift before carrying either nut again.
Lift both retained nuts clear of the table. Bring blue over its screw; keep the tilted red nut safely elevated for an orientation correction rather than attempting another tilted insertion.
Lower blue toward its screw for a closer alignment view. Tilt the elevated red grasp around the estimated nut center to correct its visibly tipped axis, with conservative continuous increments.
Blue contacted off-center, so relieve contact and shift its bore toward the visible shaft before reapproaching. Carry the reoriented red nut toward the red screw while maintaining clearance.

Continue a very slow insertion approach: refine red using the head-view offset, and lower blue with a small clockwise lead-in rather than a full tightening stroke. Watch for displacement or tracking resistance.

Bring the corrected red nut down with a small axial-centering adjustment. Blue has visibly tipped at contact, so lift it clear and move to free right-side space for a stable reset instead of forcing it.

Try a short red tightening stroke around the estimated nut center, compensating the tilted EE-to-nut offset rather than spinning about link6. Set blue down gently in clear space and release for a flat reset.

Red now shows the screw tip centered inside the nut. Finish a short clockwise stroke and release in place to test seating. Recenter blue from the head ray, straighten the approach, and close at nut height.

Red did not remain upright after release; clear the left arm rather than claim fastening. Lift the newly centered blue nut and carry it over a revised screw-axis estimate for a careful single-pair attempt.
Lower the stable blue grasp to insertion height for a closer shaft/bore check. Restore the left gripper to vertical and approach the untouched yellow nut within the left workspace.
Shift the blue bore toward the shaft visible on its left, then ease it down with a small clockwise lead-in. Center and lower the left gripper over the flat yellow nut using its top-surface ray.
Use the close wrist view to center yellow between the fingers before closing. Continue a shallow blue tightening stroke with a millimeter-scale correction toward the shaft, watching for tipping.

Head-view height correction indicates blue is still laterally offset from its screw despite apparent wrist overlap. Lift clear, shift left about 12 mm, then reapproach. Lift yellow and stage it near the middle without crossing arms.

Place yellow upright at the middle for a later right-arm pickup and clear the left gripper. Make a small blue lateral diagnostic correction at clearance, then lower only 2 mm to resolve remaining visual parallax.

The diagnostic motion moved the blue shaft toward the bore center. Continue that small lateral correction and descend 6 mm with a gentle lead-in. Withdraw the left arm from the staged yellow nut toward the red workspace.

Refine blue by only a few millimeters toward the visible tip, with a slow 6 mm axial approach and light clockwise lead-in. Hold the left arm clear while checking whether the shaft fills the bore rather than tipping the nut.
Blue now fills the bore without a visible tabletop crescent. Apply a controlled clockwise tightening stroke and shallow thread-following descent, leaving margin at the wrist joint limit.

The blue screw tip has risen well into the bore during tightening. Open in place, pause for seating, and reset wrist yaw without turning the nut backward. Verify that it stays upright before another stroke.
Blue remained upright and coaxial after release. Regrasp and add a short clockwise finishing stroke with a small axial feed, keeping the left arm clear.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no preceding motion occurred. Release blue, lift clear and start toward staged yellow while bringing the left gripper above the displaced red nut.

Bring the right gripper above the staged yellow nut with a vertical approach. Recenter the left fingers on the displaced red nut from the wrist view, close and make a short lift to assess its orientation.
Descend onto the flat staged yellow nut with a small centering correction, close, and lift to verify retention. Open and clear the left gripper after its unsuccessful red pickup.
Yellow was not retained and shifted away during closure. Reopen and move toward its observed wrist-image position while descending slowly, stopping for a centering view before closing again.
Refine the yellow grasp using the close wrist offset and corrected table-height estimate. Move a little forward and toward center, close at the nut sides, then make a short vertical retention check.

Yellow is now visibly retained with an upright bore. Lift clear and carry it above its matching screw. Bring the open left gripper closer to the red nut using the corrected scene height, stopping above contact.
Correct the rejected row from the unchanged observation. Lower yellow slowly; lift the left gripper out of contact and shift toward the red nut before a fresh, conservative approach.

Correct yellow toward the shaft occupying the left side of its bore, then add a short gentle clockwise insertion stroke. Recenter the open left gripper toward the red nut using the observed direction of image motion.

Continue yellow's gradual insertion with a tiny correction toward the visible shaft. Raise the left gripper out of renewed contact and change its jaw angle above the tipped red nut rather than forcing a downward grasp.

Yellow is tipping rather than advancing cleanly, so relieve contact and make a small isolated lateral correction without rotation. Approach the now-separated red nut from above, stopping before closure for a centering check.

The isolated motion resolved yellow's correction direction: lift clear, shift toward the shaft in the wrist view, and reapproach without twisting. Center the red nut between the fingers, close, and lift to check a recoverable grasp.

Yellow's shaft is closer to centered; continue a millimeter-scale correction with a short lead-in and shallow descent. Lift red into free space and begin rolling its sideways grasp toward an upright nut, compensating around the grasp center.

Complete the red nut's roll in free space while preserving the estimated grasp pivot. For yellow, pause twisting and test a small backward correction with brief clearance; the remaining crescent indicates lateral misalignment.

Replan from the interrupted pose: release the reoriented red nut and withdraw with smaller reverse-roll increments rather than extending the rejected motion. Yellow now appears centered; ease it down with a short clockwise engagement stroke.

Yellow tipped during the feed, so relieve contact and make a small correction toward the visible shaft without further twisting. Restore the empty left gripper toward vertical above the now-flat red nut, using a continuous reverse roll.

Use a smaller yellow feed and short tightening stroke, then release in place to test whether the nut remains upright. Center the left gripper over flat red and straighten its downward orientation before grasping.
Regrasp the now-flat red nut with small planar corrections and a short retention lift. Yellow did not remain upright; clear it with open fingers and reset wrist yaw before another approach.
The red nut is now held upright. Lift and carry it above the red shaft using the corrected height-based axis estimate, keeping the right arm safely clear while prioritizing this stable grasp.
Use the red wrist view to shift the bore toward the shaft on its right, then descend slowly without twisting. Keep the stable nut orientation and inspect alignment at the closer height.
The red shaft is now laterally centered in the wrist view. Continue a slow vertical approach without rotation, watching for the tip entering the bore before committing to a tightening stroke.

The red tip is visible in the bore with the nut still upright. Apply a modest clockwise engagement stroke with only 3 mm of axial feed, keeping the other arm clear and checking for tipping before continuing.
Corrected the rejected tensor from the unchanged pose. Relieve red contact, test a 4.5 mm backward correction without rotation, and make a shallow reapproach to assess shaft alignment.

The isolated correction moved the shaft away from the red bore. Reverse that component and add a small rightward correction to bring the shaft down the wrist image while maintaining its lateral alignment; reapproach only 2 mm.

Continue the red correction in the direction that brought its tip into the bore, with a short clockwise lead-in and shallow feed. Approach the displaced yellow nut for recovery, closing only after reaching its sides.
Corrected the rejected tensor from the unchanged observation. Make an isolated red centering correction without twisting, and withdraw the open right gripper to avoid disturbing the yellow screw.

Continue the successful direction of red centering in smaller increments, retaining brief clearance before lowering. Reapproach the yellow nut with open fingers and close at its sides; inspect retention before lifting it away.

The red tip is now almost centered within the bore; apply a slow, short tightening stroke with shallow axial feed. Lift yellow away from its screw before attempting to correct the nut's sideways orientation.

Red shifted off-axis during turning; lift clear and make a small correction toward the shaft with no further rotation. Raise the sideways yellow nut into free space and begin a slow pivot-compensated roll toward upright.

The red correction moved the shaft toward the bore center; continue only a few millimeters and reapproach without twisting. Continue yellow's slow free-space roll around the held nut, maintaining configuration continuity.

Make a small isolated red correction in the other horizontal direction to resolve the remaining bore crescent. Complete the yellow nut's free-space quarter-roll with conservative pivot-compensated increments.

Test red tightening with a small orbit compensation for the inferred link6-to-nut offset, rather than rotating at a fixed EE point. Yellow still appears edge-on; rotate slowly about the gripper's forward axis in free space to correct that remaining tilt.
Finish the short compensated red stroke, then open and pause in place to test whether it remains seated before resetting the wrist. Continue yellow's controlled forward-axis roll in free space.

Red was not retained on its screw after release; lift and reset the empty left wrist above the fallen nut. Finish yellow's free-space roll and release it for a fresh upright pickup rather than forcing the sideways grasp.
Approach the flat red nut for another centered pickup. Keep the right fingers open, let yellow settle, and restore the right arm toward a downward approach with gradual rotation and upward clearance.
The preceding chunk executed zero steps because the right IK increment was too large. Replan from the same pose with quarter-size right-arm increments, while retaining the conservative left approach.

Center the flat red nut between the jaws, close at pickup height and verify with a short lift. Continue the empty right arm's gradual recovery toward a downward approach, keeping elbow and wrist changes small.

The red nut is retained upright. Lift and move it forward over the screw using the wrist displacement, then begin a conservative descent. Continue recovering the empty right wrist toward vertical above the settled yellow nut.
Lower red with a small correction toward the shaft on the right of its bore, without tightening yet. Finish straightening the empty right wrist and approach the now-flat yellow nut with open fingers.
Red tipped on contact, so remove it from the screw and release in clear space rather than force insertion. Regrasp the flat yellow nut at the lower pickup height and make a short retention lift.

Yellow is visibly retained upright. Lift clear and carry it above the yellow shaft without changing grasp orientation. Descend the open left gripper toward the flat red nut, stopping above closure for another centering check.
Corrected the rejected row from the unchanged observation. Lift the left gripper out of contact and change its jaw angle above the red nut; lower yellow cautiously without rotation.

Straighten the left gripper and center it over the red nut with the safer jaw angle, stopping above pickup height. Yellow's tip is inside the bore; apply a small centering correction and a slow lead-in with shallow feed.

Yellow's shaft now fills the bore without a visible tabletop crescent; continue a slow tightening stroke with only 3 mm feed and wrist-limit margin. Close around the centered red nut at pickup height and make a short retention lift.

Finish a small yellow stroke, open in place, and reset wrist yaw to test seating without reverse torque. Lift the upright red nut and translate it toward the shaft using the visible planar displacement before descending again.

Yellow remained upright after opening, so regrasp and add a controlled tightening stroke. Red is aligned above its shaft; lower slowly through the remaining clearance without changing its grasp orientation.

Make a millimeter-scale red correction toward the shaft visible beside the small bore crescent, without twisting. Release yellow in place and reset wrist yaw for another tightening stroke while checking continued seating.
Yellow stayed upright after release; regrasp and add another controlled tightening stroke with a shallow thread-following descent. Apply a slower red engagement stroke now that its shaft is centered.
